rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement (Civil Code 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner shall not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice to terminate. Just cause is either at-fault cause (such as default in rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity) or no-fault cause (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government order, or intent to demolish or substantially remodel). For a curable lease violation, the owner must first give notice and an opportunity to cure.
rules.key_value: just cause required after 12 months of continuous and lawful occupancy (or, if additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months, all tenants at 12 months or more, or one or more tenants at 24 months or more)
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months; if additional adult tenants were added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, it applies only if all tenants have occupied for 12 months or more or one or more tenants for 24 months or more.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in a nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, licensed residential care facility for the elderly or adult residential facility; dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with an owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied residences (including where the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms, and mobilehomes); a two-unit property in a single structure where the owner occupied one unit at the start of the tenancy and continues in occupancy (neither unit an ADU/JADU); housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, if tenants received the required written exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households.
rules.penalty: An owner's failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs in the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages plus possible punitive damages for willful conduct or oppression, fraud, or malice. The Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: (A) Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault just cause terminations (Civil Code 1946.2(d))
rules.requirement: When an owner terminates a covered tenancy for no-fault just cause, the owner must, at the owner's option, either pay the tenant relocation assistance or waive in writing the final month's rent, equal to one month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued. Any relocation assistance must be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, and the termination notice must tell the tenant of this right.
rules.key_value: one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies for which just cause is required under subdivision (a), when the owner issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause, regardless of the tenant's income.

rules.penalty: An owner's failure to strictly comply with this subdivision renders the notice of termination void. If the tenant fails to vacate, the relocation assistance or rent waiver is recoverable as damages in an action to recover possession.
rules.quoted_span: (3) (A) The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: (C) The relocation assistance or rent waiver required by this subdivision shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.

rules.title: Tenant notice of just cause and rent cap protections (Civil Code 1946.2(f))
rules.requirement: Owners of property subject to this section must notify tenants of their rights, in the lease, an addendum, or a signed written notice for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020, and by written notice no later than August 1, 2020 or an addendum for tenancies existing before July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 and August 1, 2022 for mobilehome tenancies). The notice must be in no less than 12-point type and include the statutory statement.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to Section 1946.2.
